items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.10.12 at source lines 1399-1414, the integer induction principle with its three computation rules, proved at source lines 1415-1438. The proof does not induct on the integers: it first replaces Z by the idempotent retract Sm{x:N x N}(r(x) = x) supplied by the preceding remark (source line 1416), pulls d_0, d_+ and d_- back along the quotient map q to a family Q := P o q (lines 1418-1425), and then has to inhabit Q on all of N x N. The obstruction is the diagonal: it is closed by the fourth clause g(suc n, suc m) := e_{n,m}(g(n,m)) (line 1433), whose equivalence e_{n,m} exists only because q(n,m) = q(suc n, suc m) (lines 1426-1427). The final step needs the retraction property q o proj1 = idfunc to identify Q o proj1 with P and to build the family of equivalences s that defines f (lines 1435-1437). None of this is a routine induction on Z; the transported data and the diagonal clause are what make the three computation rules come out.
